vignette: 70-year-old man with idiopathic Parkinson's disease for 6 years, tremor-dominant form, with rest and postural tremor of the right arm plus mild rigidity of the right wrist. His tremor has responded poorly to levodopa, pramipexole and trihexyphenidyl at optimized doses, and no Hoehn and Yahr stage is recorded. Right-arm tremor is level 3 on the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin scale; he can no longer write, button shirts or use utensils with his right hand. He has a dual-chamber cardiac pacemaker for sick sinus syndrome; cardiology and the DBS team have documented a plan for device interaction precautions. MoCA 27/30, no depression, psychosis or substance use, and no major comorbidities. Requesting left thalamic VIM DBS to treat the right arm. The device is FDA-approved for DBS. A movement disorders neurologist selected the patient and will manage post-procedure care. The neurosurgeon is trained in the procedure and experienced in movement disorder surgery, including DBS, and in stereotactic neurosurgery; the operative team has DBS training, and the hospital has MRI/CT for stereotactic targeting, a stereotactic operating room, and the needed support services. The patient is willing and able to cooperate during the awake procedure and with post-operative programming and medication adjustments.
rationale_note: VIM for tremor-dominant idiopathic PD at the exact FTM boundary (level 3). Poor L-dopa response of tremor and no H&Y are irrelevant for VIM; pacemaker is a caution only.

vignette: 61-year-old woman with idiopathic Parkinson's disease for 11 years (bradykinesia, rigidity and rest tremor). Past surgery: lumbar laminectomy and a thoracic spinal cord stimulator implanted 3 years ago for radicular pain; neurosurgery has documented a plan to manage the stimulator during and after DBS. No psychosis or substance use. Requesting bilateral STN DBS. The device is FDA-approved for DBS. A movement disorders neurologist selected the patient and will manage post-procedure care. The neurosurgeon is trained in the procedure and experienced in movement disorder surgery, including DBS, and in stereotactic neurosurgery; the operative team has DBS training, and the hospital has MRI/CT for stereotactic targeting, a stereotactic operating room, and the needed support services. The patient is willing and able to cooperate during the awake procedure and with post-operative programming and medication adjustments.
rationale_note: STN DBS with distractors: remitted depression judged not to be worsened or interfere; spinal cord stimulator is an 'other electronically controlled implant' caution only; remote surgery outside the brain.
